title: Information Integrity in the Age of AI: Brazil’s Approach to Trustworthy Government Publications
raw_text: By Carla Maria Martellote Viola, Senior Researcher, Brazilian Institute of Information in Science and Technology (Ibict), Brazil As governments increasingly use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to draft, organize and deliver information, a central question is becoming unavoidable: how can the integrity of government publications be protected when generative AI is part of the information-production process? In Brazil, this issue is gaining relevance alongside the Brazilian Artificial Intelligence Plan (PBIA 2024–2028), “AI for the Good of All”, which combines technological development with social inclusion, protection of rights, information integrity and responsible AI governance [1]. Information integrity involves more than factual correctness. It depends on information being accurate, complete, reliable and sufficiently contextualized, while its origin and transformations remain traceable. In institutional environments, these attributes support transparency and public trust and help reduce the risks of error, manipulation and bias. Provenance is especially important because it allows the origin, trajectory and modifications of information to be identified and its authenticity to be assessed [2]. For government publications, where citizens may rely on official information to understand rights, policies and public services, these requirements acquire particular significance. title: From Beirut to Byblos: LAU Libraries as a Beacon of Hope
raw_text: By Caline Trad , IFLA-GIOPS -Information Coordinator and Dr. Jordan Srour, Interim Dean of Libraries and Information Resources, LAU Running three academic libraries across two campuses is not easy in normal times. The Lebanese American University Libraries are at the heart of our campuses; they are the space where students go to study, to meet, to learn, to explore, to create, to print or to just relax. With so much activity anything can and does happen on an average day…now add a war. LAU’s response to the renewal of Israeli hostilities on 2 March 2026, followed standard protocols: a rapid move to online learning . While moving learning online sounds easy it belies a reality of stress and anxiety with students afraid that their grades will be impacted because their bandwidth falters. Against this backdrop, the LAU Libraries made a commitment to remain open to ensure that all learners could come to campus to access stable internet and electricity. Again, not an easy decision. Opening the libraries meant requiring staff to be present on campus – even in the face of streets that were crowded with displaced Lebanese, fuel prices that multiplied, and drones that circled – and still circle – overhead. War altered the meaning of librarianship inside the three LAU libraries. Unique in the design of the Riyad Nassar Library (RNL) in Beirut, is the fact that it doubles as an airstrike shelter. title: From North to South: Lebanon Rising from the Ashes
raw_text: By Caline Trad , IFLA-GIOPS -Information Coordinator Lebanon has always been much more than a country – from North to South it is a cradle of civilization, a mosaic of faiths and a land of resilience. Lebanon’s identity is woven with pluralism, with 18 sects recognized among Christian, Islam and Druze communities. This balance is also reflected in its political system, where at the highest level of government is a Christian president and a Sunni Muslim Prime Minister, emblematic of coexistence. This diversity, though often tested, is a source of strength and cultural richness. Throughout its long history, Lebanon has offered the world treasures of intellect and spirit: from the Phoenicians who carried trade and culture across the Mediterranean, to Gibran Khalil Gibran whose words turned Beirut into a beacon of inspiration, to Fairuz whose voice is the heartbeat of a nation. On a modest stretch of just 10,452 square km, mountains guarding over generations, posts welcoming travelers, and its people rising after every storm form the land of resilience where the Lebanese spirit never dies. From Byblos, where the first alphabet was born and took shape, to the cedar forests praised in scripture, Lebanon has stood as a sanctuary of saints and prophets, a land where churches and mosques rise side by side, and where faith and culture intertwine. title: MetLib 2026 | Day 1: Libraries in a World Shaped by Technology
raw_text: The first day of the Metropolitan Libraries Conference (MetLib 2026) in the Netherlands brought together library professionals from around the world to explore some of the most pressing questions facing our cities and societies. The key themes of the conference were introduced during the opening speeches and an inspiring keynote by artist Julia Janssen , focusing on the growing influence of technology on our lives. During our visit to The Hague Public Library, the director Sam Hermans , welcoming participants on behalf of the G4 cities organising the conference, emphasised that technology is already transforming the future of our cities. In this changing environment, libraries must remain places of connection, bringing people together and strengthening communities. In her thought-provoking keynote, Julia Janssen explored how algorithms increasingly shape our everyday lives, often without us even realising it. Through four examples from her artistic work, she demonstrated how digital technologies can reinforce the power of profit-driven corporations and gradually undermine our ability to think critically and question the systems around us. One of her most compelling messages was the need to demystify artificial intelligence — perhaps starting by calling it what it really is: automation . title: Sharing Session in Brunei by Ms Tina Yang, University of Hong Kong
raw_text: Ms Tina Yang, Associate Librarian from the University of Hong Kong, visited Brunei from 24 to 27 August 2026. The Brunei Darussalam Library Association (BLA) coordinated her visits to several libraries, including Universiti Brunei Darussalam, Universiti Teknologi Brunei, Brunei Islamic Library, and Universiti Islam Sultan Sharif Ali. Image 1 – Ms Tina Yang and members of the BLA. During her stay, Ms Yang delivered two sharing sessions — the first on 26 August 2026 to students of the Diploma in Information and Library Studies at the School of ICT, IBTE SSR Campus, and the second on 27 August 2026 at DBP Brunei for librarians from various libraries. Image 2 – Sharing session by Ms Tina Yang BLA also held an informal meeting with Ms Tina to exchange experiences and explore ideas for possible future collaboration between Brunei and Hong Kong. title: Seam Cutter
raw_text: Tool: Seam Cutter I built this weird and very specific cropping tool - it lets you create a horizontal or vertical cut across an image, then slide the two sides relative to each other. Effectively it lets you crop out a section in the middle of an image. I wanted this because I often use Tailor on my iPhone to stitch several screenshots together into lot long image, but sometimes I find myself wanting to crop out a section in the middle - to redact an irrelevant prompt from a transcript, for example. Goedkoper en meer controle: bedrijven kijken met interesse naar Chinese AI
raw_text: Wat als je AI goedkoper kunt gebruiken én je de controle houdt over de informatie die je deelt? Bedrijven en organisaties die werken met AI-technologie kijken daarvoor met veel interesse naar open AI-modellen, die vooral door Chinese bedrijven worden gemaakt. Terwijl de grote Amerikaanse AI-bedrijven zoals Anthropic, OpenAI en Google abonnementskosten vragen en kosten rekenen voor het gebruik van hun krachtigste gesloten AI-modellen, zijn de open AI-modellen gratis te downloaden. Gebruikers kunnen daardoor zelf kiezen op welke servers een open AI-model draait, terwijl bij gesloten modellen de maker bepaalt. Dat kan risicovol zijn als je persoonlijke of gevoelige informatie wil verwerken met een gesloten AI-model: die gegevens worden verwerkt op computerapparatuur die je zelf niet beheert. De populairste open AI-modellen worden gemaakt door Chinese bedrijven zoals Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot en Z.ai. Ook een aantal Amerikaanse bedrijven brengt open AI-modellen uit, waaronder Meta, het bedrijf achter Facebook en Instagram. Veel interesse in open AI-modellen Het advocatenkantoor Driven Lawyers in Amsterdam maakt daar dankbaar gebruik van. Show HN: Hurston-1 open source TTS that speak Southern American and Afro-English
raw_text: Hey HN, I’m open sourcing my Hurston-1 narrowband TTS model (Apache-2.0). It is very good with American English and does especially well with Southern American and Regional African English accents. Destined AI is based in Atlanta, and I built this because I’m amazed by what AI can do, and I wanted to help introduce and welcome more people to feel comfortable using and interacting with AI. Since 2021, I’ve been collecting fully consented voice data from over 20,000 people, 1M audio recordings, and over 1,800 hrs of audio captured to date. For this model, I used a small part of the data, 136 hrs, to finetune Maya1 and expand it’s capabilities. Hurston-1 is a narrowband TTS model that focuses the output on telephone use because that is still where most of these voices will be heard. I’ve used it to support customers such as Amazon and Salesforce and generated over half-mill revenue with it. Now I’m open sourcing it to help unlock opportunities for others as well. Limitations: this model doesn’t maintain the exact same voice across prompts and doesn’t support voice cloning. For many use cases, this is fine but maybe not so - if you’re creating podcasts. This is the first release - I’m already working on the next version with improvements. I would appreciate, if anyone is interested in this space, download the model from huggingface, check it out and let me know any feedback. Also, open to connecting with others in this space as well.

title: Scott Walker’s The Drift will get under your skin
raw_text: In my mind, Spooky Season music comes in two distinct flavors. There are the fun, occasionally goofy songs like "The Monster Mash" and John Carpenter's "Halloween Theme." Then there is the genuinely terrifying: Throbbing Gristle , The Body , or Scott Walker's The Drift . This 2006 album from the singer-songwriter is truly upsetting. On it, Walker explores death, disease, and tragedy. But not just from some abstract perspective. There are visceral descriptions of the hanging of Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci.
